posts.text:
Good to see bipartisan legislation pass in the Minnesota House and Senate. After Colin Hortman shared his story, this bill requires disclosure of chemical irritants and helps ensure homeowners aren’t stuck with the clean-up cost by their insurance.

duluthnewstribune.com/news/m…

Brit’s Pub is a true Minneapolis staple of British food and culture. It was great to have invited Brit’s general manager, Shane Higgins, to King Charles’ address to Congress.

Video

The impact of the administration’s war with Iran will be long-lasting. Higher energy and fertilizer costs are rippling through our economy — hitting Minnesota farmers hard and raising prices for Americans, with no clear plan ahead.

mprnews.org/story/2026/04/28…

This Court ruling weakens protections against discrimination & undermines fair representation. As Justice Kagan said, it marks the “majority’s now-completed demolition of the Voting Rights Act.”

We must keep fighting so every American has a voice in our democracy.
King Charles, in his speech, highlighted our shared democratic roots and the bedrock principle that executive power must be subject to checks and balances.

In Faribault, I met with Sheriff Thomas and the County Board to see the new Rice County Public Safety Center. This state-of-the-art facility will strengthen public safety and support the important work of law enforcement.

southernminn.com/faribault_d…
At Inver Hills Community College, I got to meet students gaining hands-on experience that will prepare them to step into good-paying jobs that are in high demand across Minnesota.

Invited a fitting guest for King Charles’s address to Congress: Shane Higgins, the dedicated general manager behind one of our state’s favorite British traditions — Brit’s Pub. Great to have him in Washington today, representing a bit of the UK from Minnesota. 🇺🇸🇬🇧

Costs are up. Tariffs are hurting our farmers and small businesses. And this war is driving up gas and fertilizer prices. We need to stop the chaos and focus on making things affordable for Americans.

Video

82-year-old Anita LeBrun of Champlin showed up at the State Capitol and helped pass the “Grandparents Happy Hour” bill. Cheers to a job well done, Anita!

startribune.com/champlin-82-…

20,000 teddy bears on the National Mall representing the 20,000 Ukrainian children taken from their families by Putin’s brutal invasion. 

We must stand with Ukraine. 

We are here. 🇺🇸 🇺🇦

Video

First responders need the tools to act quickly in emergencies. This new Mobile Command Center in Eden Prairie will improve coordination and response times to strengthen public safety. That’s why I worked to secure federal funding for this vital project.

eplocalnews.org/2026/04/10/e…

After 80 years, Capt. Willibald “Bill” Bianchi finally returned home to New Ulm. A Minnesota farm kid who became a Medal of Honor hero. His courage and sacrifice will never be forgotten.

startribune.com/missing-for-…

Good to see a unanimous, bipartisan vote to toughen penalties for impersonating law enforcement.

After the horrific murder of Melissa and Mark Hortman and the attack on John Hoffman and his family, we must come together to take action.

cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/m…

Great to see so many people this week out supporting Mid-Minnesota Legal Aid — an organization that provides legal services to Minnesotans in need. 

Thank you to keynote speaker Neal Katyal, whose commitment to the rule of law inspires lawyers across the country.
Glad everyone—including the President and the First Lady and all journalists—are safe at the White House Correspondents’ dinner.

At the Inver Hills Community College to tour the new simulation lab with President Berndt. I worked to secure funding for this lab, which is now helping train the next generation of Minnesota health care workers and connecting them to jobs.

It was a beautiful night in St. Paul at the Harriet Island Pavilion for Mayor Kaohly Her's Inaugural Celebration, with a fitting theme of “Rising Together.” As St. Paul’s first woman and Hmong American mayor, she is making history.
